strategies.name: Trend following
strategies.idea: Prices that have been rising tend to keep rising for a while ('the trend is your friend'). The strategy rides established directional moves instead of predicting reversals.

rules.entry: Join the existing direction: e.g., buy when price holds above a rising long-term moving average after a pullback.
rules.exit: Trail the stop behind the trend and let winners run; exit when the trend breaks (e.g., close below the trend line / average).
rules.stop: Below the most recent swing low (long) or a volatility-based distance such as 2x ATR.

strategies.pros: Simple, captures the biggest moves, works across many markets.
strategies.fails: Sideways/ranging markets cause repeated small losses ('whipsaws'); late entries when the trend is exhausted.
strategies.risk: Expect many small losses between a few large wins — psychology, not math, is the hard part.

strategies.name: Breakout trading
strategies.idea: When price escapes a well-defined range or level (support/resistance, prior high/low), stored energy releases and a new move often begins.

rules.entry: Enter after a close beyond the level, ideally with above-average volume confirming.
rules.exit: Target measured moves (e.g., range height projected from the breakout) or trail the stop.
rules.stop: Just back inside the broken range — if price returns, the breakout failed.

strategies.pros: Clear levels, clear invalidation; catches moves early.
strategies.fails: False breakouts ('fakeouts') are common, especially on low volume or into news.
strategies.risk: Chasing extended breakouts without waiting for the close is the classic beginner trap.

strategies.name: Pullback / retest entries
strategies.idea: Instead of chasing, wait for a trending market to dip to a known level (old resistance turns support, a rising moving average) and enter there at a better price with a closer stop.

rules.entry: After the pullback reaches the level and shows rejection (e.g., a bullish candle at support in an uptrend).
rules.exit: Previous swing high first, then trail the stop under rising swing lows.
rules.stop: Beyond the level being tested — if it gives way, the idea is wrong.

strategies.pros: Better prices and tighter, logical stops than chasing.
strategies.fails: Strong trends sometimes never pull back; weak trends 'pull back' all the way into reversal.
strategies.risk: Distinguishing a healthy pullback from the start of a reversal is judgment, not certainty.

strategies.name: Range trading & mean reversion
strategies.idea: In a sideways market, price oscillates between support and resistance and tends to return toward its average. Buy near support, sell near resistance, fade extremes.

rules.entry: At the range edges with confirmation (rejection candle, oscillator extreme).
rules.exit: Mid-range (the mean) first, opposite edge second.
rules.stop: Outside the range — a close beyond it means the regime changed.

strategies.pros: Frequent, well-defined setups; clear levels both ways.
strategies.fails: Ranges eventually break — one breakout against you can erase many small range wins.
strategies.risk: Never 'average down' a broken range without a predefined maximum loss.

strategies.name: RSI momentum & extremes
strategies.idea: The Relative Strength Index (0-100) measures speed of recent gains vs losses. Readings above 70 / below 30 flag stretched conditions; in trends, pullbacks to RSI 40-50 (uptrend) mark continuation zones.

rules.entry: Two textbook styles: (a) fade extremes only inside ranges; (b) in trends, enter when RSI resets to mid-zone and turns back with price.
rules.exit: Opposite extreme, or price-based targets (prior swing).
rules.stop: Beyond the swing that created the RSI signal.

strategies.pros: Objective overbought/oversold gauge; divergence warns of weakening moves.
strategies.fails: In strong trends RSI can stay 'overbought' for weeks — fading it blindly is expensive.
strategies.risk: RSI is a thermometer, not a steering wheel: it describes, it does not predict.

strategies.name: MACD crossover & histogram
strategies.idea: MACD compares two exponential moving averages (12 vs 26). Crossovers of the MACD line and its 9-period signal line mark momentum shifts; the histogram visualizes their distance.

rules.entry: Long when MACD crosses up through the signal line (stronger below/near the zero line in an uptrend context).
rules.exit: Opposite crossover, histogram shrinking after extension, or price targets.
rules.stop: Beyond the swing low/high preceding the crossover.

strategies.pros: Combines trend + momentum in one panel; divergence is a useful warning.
strategies.fails: Lagging and noisy in ranges — crossovers whipsaw sideways markets.
strategies.risk: Because it is built from averages, MACD always confirms AFTER price has moved.

strategies.name: Bollinger Band squeeze
strategies.idea: Bollinger Bands (20-period average ±2 standard deviations) widen with volatility and contract in quiet markets. Extreme contraction ('the squeeze') often precedes an expansion move — direction unknown.

rules.entry: Wait for the expansion: a strong close outside the band after a squeeze, trade in that direction.
rules.exit: Ride while closes stay outside/near the band ('walking the band'); exit when momentum closes back inside.
rules.stop: Middle band (the 20-period average) or the squeeze's opposite edge.

strategies.pros: Objective volatility regime detector; adapts to market speed.
strategies.fails: The squeeze says 'something is coming', never which way; first expansion can reverse violently.
strategies.risk: Touching a band is not by itself a reversal signal — in trends price hugs bands.

strategies.name: Moving-average cross (golden / death cross)
strategies.idea: A faster average (e.g., 50-day) crossing above a slower one (200-day) is called a golden cross; below, a death cross. A slow regime filter more than a precise trigger.

rules.entry: Favor longs while price and the fast average sit above the slow average; favor defense/cash below.
rules.exit: Opposite cross, or use crosses only as a bias filter for other entries.
rules.stop: System-level: the opposite cross IS the exit — per-trade stops still apply.

strategies.pros: Keeps you on the right side of major trends; trivially backtestable.
strategies.fails: Very lagging — by the cross, much of the move happened; sideways years whipsaw it.
strategies.risk: A filter reduces (never removes) drawdowns; past index behavior is not a guarantee.

strategies.name: Support & resistance (horizontal levels)
strategies.idea: Markets remember levels where price previously reversed or stalled. Those zones attract orders again, so trades are planned around them rather than in empty space.

rules.entry: Buy support / sell resistance with a confirmation candle, or trade the break-and-retest.
rules.stop: Just beyond the level — beyond it, the level failed.

strategies.pros: The foundation under almost every other strategy; no indicators needed.
strategies.fails: Levels are zones, not laser lines; they weaken with each test and break without warning.
strategies.risk: Drawing a level does not obligate the market to respect it.

strategies.name: Fibonacci retracement
strategies.idea: After an impulse move, pullbacks often pause near 38.2%, 50%, or 61.8% of that move. Traders watch those proportional zones for trend-continuation entries.

rules.entry: In the 50-61.8% zone ('golden pocket') when it aligns with structure (old level, average) and a rejection appears.
rules.exit: Prior swing extreme, then extension levels (127%, 161.8%).
rules.stop: Beyond the next retracement level or the impulse origin.

strategies.pros: Gives planned, proportional entry zones instead of chasing.
strategies.fails: Self-fulfilling at best; weak trends retrace 100%+. Three zones means one usually 'works' — selection bias.
strategies.risk: Ratios are conventions, not physics. Confluence with structure matters more than the decimal.

strategies.name: VWAP intraday
strategies.idea: VWAP is the day's volume-weighted average price — the level institutions benchmark fills against. Intraday traders use it as a fair-value magnet and bias line.

rules.entry: Trend day: buy pullbacks to a rising VWAP. Range day: fade moves 2+ standard-deviation bands away from VWAP back toward it.
rules.exit: VWAP itself (mean trades) or band extensions (trend trades). Flat by the close.
rules.stop: Beyond the band/level that defined the setup; time-based exit before close.

strategies.pros: Objective, widely watched intraday reference; resets daily so no stale levels.
strategies.fails: Requires volume data and screen time; news days ignore VWAP entirely.
strategies.risk: Intraday trading has the highest cost drag (spread+fees) — most day traders lose.

strategies.name: Gap-and-go (opening momentum)
strategies.idea: A stock gapping on real news with heavy pre-market volume sometimes continues in the gap direction during the opening range as institutions reposition.

rules.entry: After the first minutes form an opening range; enter on its break in the gap direction with volume surging.
rules.exit: Fast, into opening momentum; most gap trades are done within the first hour.
rules.stop: Opening-range opposite edge — gaps that fill immediately are failed ideas.

strategies.pros: Concentrated opportunity window; news provides a genuine catalyst.
strategies.fails: Many gaps fade and fill; spreads and slippage are widest exactly then.
strategies.risk: Fastest way for a beginner to lose: emotional, leveraged, wide spreads. Paper-trade extensively.

strategies.name: Pairs trading (statistical basics)
strategies.idea: Two historically related instruments (e.g., two banks) tend to keep a stable price relationship. When the spread stretches far from its average, buy the laggard and short the leader, betting on the relationship — not direction.

rules.entry: When the spread's z-score exceeds a threshold (textbooks use ±2) after checking the pair is still fundamentally linked.
rules.exit: Spread returns toward its mean (z near 0).
rules.stop: A wider z (e.g., ±3-4) or any fundamental break in one leg (earnings disaster, merger).

strategies.pros: Market-direction neutral in theory; the rationale is statistical, testable.
strategies.fails: Relationships break permanently ('the spread can stay irrational longer…'); borrow costs on the short leg.
strategies.risk: Correlation is not a contract. Cointegration can vanish exactly when you size up.

strategies.name: Forex carry basics
strategies.idea: Borrow a low-interest currency, hold a higher-interest one, and earn the rate difference ('swap'). The return is the interest — the risk is the exchange rate moving against you more than the carry earned.

rules.entry: Textbook version pairs the carry with a supportive trend/risk environment and modest leverage.
rules.exit: When rate differentials shrink, volatility spikes, or the trend breaks.
rules.stop: Position-level risk limits; carry trades historically unwind violently in crises.

strategies.pros: A real, well-documented long-term factor in currency markets.
strategies.fails: 'Picking up pennies in front of a steamroller': calm gains, sudden crash losses (2008, 2020).
strategies.risk: Leverage turns a slow interest trickle into a fast margin call. This is a professional strategy.

strategies.name: Dollar-cost averaging & value averaging
strategies.idea: Invest a fixed amount on a fixed schedule regardless of market noise. You automatically buy more units when prices are low and fewer when high, removing timing decisions.

rules.entry: Automatic fixed contributions (e.g., monthly) into diversified holdings.
rules.exit: Goal-based (retirement, house deposit), with periodic rebalancing — not headlines.
rules.stop: None per-trade; risk is managed by diversification, horizon, and keeping an emergency fund outside the market.

strategies.pros: The approach with the strongest evidence for ordinary savers; behaviorally robust.
strategies.fails: Sitting through -30% drawdowns is emotionally hard; single-stock DCA can ride a failing company to zero.
strategies.risk: Still not a guarantee: markets can fall for years. Diversification and horizon do the heavy lifting.

strategies.name: Catalyst / earnings momentum
strategies.idea: Genuine news (earnings beats, raised guidance, regulatory approvals) re-prices a stock, and the repricing often drifts over days/weeks ('post-earnings-announcement drift', a documented academic effect).

rules.entry: After the initial reaction day, on strength in the news direction once a base/pullback forms — not into the first chaotic spike.
rules.exit: As volume and momentum normalize, or at predefined targets.
rules.stop: Below the post-news base; if the market rejects the news, leave.

strategies.pros: Grounded in a real, studied market phenomenon; news gives a 'why'.
strategies.fails: 'Buy the rumor, sell the news' — good news already priced in gets sold into.
strategies.risk: Event risk cuts both ways: secondary offerings, lawsuits, or guidance cuts can gap through stops.

methods.name: Price action & market structure
methods.summary: Reading raw price: higher highs/lows (uptrend), lower highs/lows (downtrend), breaks of structure, and reactions at prior swing points. The grammar every other method annotates.
methods.tools: Swing points, trend lines, horizontal levels, candlestick rejection wicks.
methods.watch_out: Structure is fractal — an uptrend on 5-minutes can sit inside a weekly downtrend. State your timeframe or fool yourself.

methods.name: Candlestick patterns
methods.summary: Single- and multi-candle shapes (engulfing, pin bar, doji, morning star…) that summarize who won the session's battle between buyers and sellers.
methods.tools: The illustrated patterns in this atlas; always read location (at support/resistance) over shape alone.
methods.watch_out: A pattern in the middle of nowhere means little; the same candle at a major level means more. Context first, names second.

methods.name: Chart patterns
methods.summary: Larger formations — triangles, flags, head-and-shoulders, double tops/bottoms, wedges — that frame consolidation vs continuation and give measured-move targets.
methods.tools: Trend lines, necklines, measured moves (pattern height projected from the break).
methods.watch_out: Patterns are in the eye of the beholder until they break; trade the break + retest, not the hope.

methods.name: Indicator analysis
methods.summary: Mathematical transformations of price/volume: moving averages (trend), RSI/Stochastic (momentum), MACD (both), ATR (volatility for stops/position sizing), Bollinger Bands (volatility envelope).
methods.tools: One tool per job: trend filter, timing aid, volatility gauge. Fewer, understood deeply, beat ten stacked randomly.
methods.watch_out: Every indicator is derived from price — it cannot know more than price. Lag is the price of smoothness.

methods.name: Volume analysis
methods.summary: Volume shows conviction: breakouts on expanding volume, pullbacks on shrinking volume, climax volume at exhaustions, and volume profile (where most trading actually happened).
methods.tools: Volume bars vs their average, OBV, VWAP, volume-profile high/low volume nodes.
methods.watch_out: Forex 'volume' from a broker is tick count, not true volume; crypto volume varies wildly by exchange.

methods.name: Order-flow basics
methods.summary: Watching the actual bid/ask battle: order book (Level 2), time & sales, and footprint/delta concepts used by futures day traders.
methods.tools: Depth of market, tape speed, cumulative delta. Mostly an intraday, futures-centric craft.
methods.watch_out: Spoofing and hidden iceberg orders mean the book can lie; tools and data feeds for this usually cost money.

methods.name: Fundamental analysis
methods.summary: Valuing the underlying business/economy: revenue growth, margins, cash flow, debt, moat, management; for macro assets: rates, inflation, growth, central-bank policy.
methods.tools: Income statement, balance sheet, cash-flow statement; ratios (P/E, ROE, debt/equity); earnings quality checks.
methods.watch_out: A great company can be a terrible stock if the price already assumes perfection. Value and price are different questions.

methods.name: Macro & sentiment analysis
methods.summary: Positioning and mood: interest-rate expectations, fear/greed gauges, put/call ratios, COT reports, fund flows. Extremes of one-sided positioning precede reversals — timing them is the art.
methods.tools: Central-bank calendars, CPI/jobs releases, VIX, COT (Commitment of Traders) data.
methods.watch_out: Sentiment can stay extreme far longer than a leveraged account can stay solvent. Extremes warn; price confirms.

methods.name: Intermarket analysis
methods.summary: Markets move in families: dollar vs commodities, yields vs growth stocks, risk-on vs risk-off currencies, credit spreads vs equities. Cross-checking relatives confirms or questions a move.
methods.tools: Correlation checks across DXY, yields, gold, oil, major indices before committing to a narrative.
methods.watch_out: Correlations are regime-dependent; in panics, 'everything correlates to 1' — diversification fails exactly when wanted most.

methods.name: Backtesting & trade journaling
methods.summary: The scientific layer: test a rule-set on historical data (including costs), then journal live trades — setup, size, exit, emotion — and review expectancy per setup, not per opinion.
methods.tools: Spreadsheet or code backtests, walk-forward checks, a trade journal with expectancy = win% × avg win − loss% × avg loss.
methods.watch_out: Overfitting: tuning rules until history looks perfect guarantees the future disappoints. Out-of-sample honesty or it didn't happen.

patterns.name: Bullish engulfing
patterns.read: A red candle followed by a green candle whose body completely covers the prior body: buyers overwhelmed sellers in one session.

patterns.name: Bearish engulfing
patterns.read: A green candle engulfed by a red one: sellers took the session back. Most meaningful after a run-up into resistance.

patterns.name: Hammer (pin bar at lows)
patterns.read: Price plunged intraday but closed near the open, leaving a long lower wick: the dip was bought. At support after a decline, it warns sellers are tiring.

patterns.name: Shooting star
patterns.read: A long upper wick after an advance: buyers pushed up, sellers pushed it all back by the close. The mirror image of the hammer.

patterns.name: Doji
patterns.read: Open and close nearly equal despite a wide range: neither side won. After a long trend it hints momentum is stalling — it is a question, not an answer.

patterns.name: Morning star (3-candle)
patterns.read: Strong red candle, small indecisive candle, strong green candle closing deep into the first: a three-act handover from sellers to buyers.

patterns.name: Evening star (3-candle)
patterns.read: The morning star inverted: strong advance, pause, then a strong red candle. A handover from buyers to sellers at highs.

patterns.name: Inside bar
patterns.read: A candle fully inside the previous candle's range: volatility contracted. Traders watch which side of the mother bar breaks first — with the trend preferred.

risk_rules.title: Risk a tiny fixed fraction per trade
risk_rules.detail: Textbooks suggest risking about 0.5-2% of the account per idea, so a losing streak is survivable math, not ruin. Position size is derived FROM the stop distance — never the other way around.

risk_rules.title: The stop is part of the idea
risk_rules.detail: Decide before entry where you are proven wrong. A stop that gets moved 'just a bit further' is not risk management; it is hope with extra steps.

risk_rules.title: Expectancy over win-rate
risk_rules.detail: A system can win 40% of the time and profit (big wins, small losses) or win 80% and lose (tiny wins, rare disasters). Track expectancy in R: (win% × avg win) − (loss% × avg loss).

risk_rules.title: Costs are a strategy filter
risk_rules.detail: Spread + commission + slippage tax every trade. Hyperactive strategies must overcome a wall of friction before any edge shows.

risk_rules.title: Leverage multiplies everything
risk_rules.detail: Leverage scales gains, losses, AND the speed of ruin. Liquidation math does not care about your analysis being eventually right.

risk_rules.title: Correlation is hidden size
risk_rules.detail: Five positions that all move together are one big position. Cap total open risk, not just per-trade risk.

risk_rules.title: Drawdowns are the real exam
risk_rules.detail: Every strategy in this atlas has losing stretches. If a -20% equity dip would make you abandon or revenge-trade, the size was already too big.

risk_rules.title: Journal or it didn't happen
risk_rules.detail: Memory edits history. A written journal (setup, size, exit reason, screenshot) is how 'experience' becomes measurable instead of anecdotal.

glossary.definition: Average True Range — typical bar size over N periods; used to set volatility-aware stops and sizes.
Applying fixed rules to historical data to see how they would have behaved — then distrusting the result appropriately.
What buyers offer / sellers ask / the gap between them — the first cost of every trade.
Peak-to-trough decline of an account or strategy; the pain metric that ends most trading careers.
Average profit per trade over many trades: (win% × avg win) − (loss% × avg loss). Positive or the rest is decoration.
How easily size trades without moving the price. Illiquid = wide spreads and exits that vanish in stress.
Profit/loss measured in units of initial risk. A +2R win made twice what was risked.
Distance to stop vs distance to target. 1:2 means risking 1 to aim for 2 — before costs and reality.
Difference between expected and actual fill price, worst in fast markets and around news.
A predefined exit that limits loss when the idea is wrong. Gaps can jump through stops — they limit, not guarantee.
Zones where price previously paused or reversed and where resting orders cluster.
How much price moves. High volatility = opportunity and danger in equal measure; position size must shrink as it rises.

goals.title: Focus research and the bot on 1m/5m/15m bars
goals.evidence: Seven minute engines, a 1/3/5/15/30-bar hidden-future race, minute bot defaults and 1m public-data presets.

goals.title: Reach at least 80% out-of-sample direction accuracy
goals.current_real_evidence: v13 real daily/monthly samples reached 68% on one AAPL test and 63.077% pooled; no bundled real minute sample establishes a minute rate.

goals.title: Become a complete real trading bot
goals.implemented: Minute paper bot, risk halts, Start/Resume/Pause/STOP/flatten workflow and manual external execution tickets.
goals.not_implemented: No exchange/broker credentials, API-key storage, automatic order routing, leverage or shorting in TradeAtlas.
goals.next_gate: A separately reviewed testnet integration in the user's own licensed account would require security, legal, venue and halal-form review before any live automation.

goals.title: Let the user fund trading with USDT or BTC
goals.rule: USDT/BTC remain in the user's own licensed exchange account. TradeAtlas has no deposit address and must never receive or custody crypto.
goals.implemented: External-account balance mirror and paper conversion/transfer simulations; the mirror is user-reported and is not added to paper equity.

goals.title: Collect and store lawful market data by itself
goals.evidence: Allowlisted public-venue collector (server CLI and browser), incremental SQLite storage with provenance, holdout reservation with a recorded access count, pooled evidence and a gate-by-gate goal report.
goals.not_claimed: Automation increases sample size and honesty, not accuracy. goal_established stays false in every code path.

goals.title: Learn from every failed test instead of repeating it
goals.evidence: A cause library of 20 named failure modes, an avoid-rule and an implemented remedy per cause, a three-stage loop (screen -> apply lessons -> validate), resolved/recurred/retired lesson states, and a SQLite failure memory that makes later runs skip already-proven dead candidates.
goals.not_claimed: The failure memory improves the *research process*, not the market. It cannot create an edge that the sample does not contain, and it never lowers the 80% gates.

goals.title: Keep bot entries behind current halal evidence
goals.rule: Only registered assets whose current screen is exactly pass may enter even a paper/manual-ticket workflow.

project_goals.warning: Goals are not performance claims. Do not send money or crypto to TradeAtlas.

market_lab.name: TradeAtlas Market Lab

ma_cross.name: EMA 20/50 cross
ma_cross.long_rule: EMA20 crosses above EMA50 at bar close.
ma_cross.short_rule: EMA20 crosses below EMA50 at bar close.

macd_cross.name: MACD signal cross
macd_cross.long_rule: MACD (12,26) crosses above its 9-period signal line.
macd_cross.short_rule: MACD crosses below its signal line.

breakout_20.name: 20-bar breakout
breakout_20.long_rule: Close breaks above the highest high of the prior 20 bars.
breakout_20.short_rule: Close breaks below the lowest low of the prior 20 bars.

rsi_reversal.name: RSI extreme reversal
rsi_reversal.long_rule: RSI(14) crosses back above 30 after being oversold.
rsi_reversal.short_rule: RSI(14) crosses back below 70 after being overbought.

bollinger_mean_reversion.name: Bollinger mean reversion
bollinger_mean_reversion.atlas_strategy: Range trading & mean reversion / Bollinger Bands
bollinger_mean_reversion.long_rule: Close returns inside the lower Bollinger Band after closing below it.
bollinger_mean_reversion.short_rule: Close returns inside the upper Bollinger Band after closing above it.

trend_pullback_rsi.name: Trend pullback + RSI reset
trend_pullback_rsi.long_rule: Close is above SMA50 and RSI crosses upward through 45.
trend_pullback_rsi.short_rule: Close is below SMA50 and RSI crosses downward through 55.

consensus.name: Multi-indicator consensus
consensus.long_rule: Consensus score rises to +3 or higher (EMA trend, MACD, RSI, price vs SMA50).
consensus.short_rule: Consensus score falls to -3 or lower.

stochastic_reversal.name: Stochastic zone reversal
stochastic_reversal.long_rule: Stochastic %K crosses above %D while %D is in the oversold zone (<= 30).
stochastic_reversal.short_rule: Stochastic %K crosses below %D while %D is in the overbought zone (>= 70).

adx_trend_strength.name: ADX trend-strength onset
adx_trend_strength.long_rule: ADX(14) crosses above 25 while +DI is above -DI (a measurable uptrend is starting).
adx_trend_strength.short_rule: ADX(14) crosses above 25 while -DI is above +DI (a measurable downtrend is starting).

schaff_cycle.name: Schaff Trend Cycle turn
schaff_cycle.long_rule: STC crosses upward through 25 after a cycle washout.
schaff_cycle.short_rule: STC crosses downward through 75 after a cycle peak.

fisher_reversal.name: Fisher Transform reversal
fisher_reversal.long_rule: Fisher crosses above its one-bar trigger while still below zero (turning up from the low side).
fisher_reversal.short_rule: Fisher crosses below its one-bar trigger while still above zero (turning down from the high side).

kst_momentum.name: KST momentum cross
kst_momentum.long_rule: KST crosses above its 9-bar signal average.
kst_momentum.short_rule: KST crosses below its 9-bar signal average.

entropy_trend.name: Entropy-gated multiscale trend (TradeAtlas research rule)
entropy_trend.atlas_strategy: Invented v10 Entropy-Weighted Trend: vol-normalized 3/5/10/20/60/120-bar momentum, gated by permutation entropy of smoothed log price
entropy_trend.long_rule: Entropy-Weighted Trend crosses above +0.10 while 60-bar permutation entropy is <= 0.80 (ordered, not noise-dominated).
entropy_trend.short_rule: Entropy-Weighted Trend crosses below -0.10 while 60-bar permutation entropy is <= 0.80.

cci_reversal.name: CCI extreme reversal
cci_reversal.long_rule: CCI(20) crosses back above -100 after an downside extreme.
cci_reversal.short_rule: CCI(20) crosses back below +100 after an upside extreme.

parabolic_sar_trend.name: Parabolic SAR flip
parabolic_sar_trend.long_rule: Parabolic SAR flips from above price to below price.
parabolic_sar_trend.short_rule: Parabolic SAR flips from below price to above price.

ichimoku_cloud.name: Ichimoku cloud state
ichimoku_cloud.atlas_strategy: Ichimoku Tenkan/Kijun plus the cloud projected from past bars
ichimoku_cloud.long_rule: Ichimoku score crosses above +1/3 (price/cloud/Tenkan-Kijun confluence turns positive).

kalman_trend.name: Kalman local-trend slope
kalman_trend.atlas_strategy: Causal alpha-beta/Kalman-style local linear trend filter on log price
kalman_trend.long_rule: Bounded Kalman log-price slope crosses above +0.15.
kalman_trend.short_rule: Bounded Kalman log-price slope crosses below -0.15.

omni_consensus.name: Omni direct consensus (TradeAtlas v11)
omni_consensus.atlas_strategy: Fixed weighted fusion of multiscale trend, Kalman slope, horizon-matched trend, Parabolic SAR and an oscillator basket

hull_trend.name: Hull moving-average trend
hull_trend.atlas_strategy: Alan Hull moving average (low-lag weighted MA combination)
hull_trend.long_rule: ATR-normalized Hull trend score crosses above +0.20.
hull_trend.short_rule: ATR-normalized Hull trend score crosses below -0.20.

supertrend_flip.name: Supertrend flip
supertrend_flip.long_rule: Supertrend flips from above price to below price.
supertrend_flip.short_rule: Supertrend flips from below price to above price.

kaufman_trend.name: Kaufman adaptive trend
kaufman_trend.atlas_strategy: Kaufman Adaptive Moving Average efficiency-ratio trend

haar_wavelet.name: Haar wavelet multiscale trend
haar_wavelet.atlas_strategy: Haar block-average wavelet decomposition over 4/8/16/32/64 bars
haar_wavelet.long_rule: Volatility-normalized Haar trend score crosses above +0.20.

data_guide.step: 1. Export real bars you already have a right to use
data_guide.detail: Broker/exchange history export, TradingView chart data export (paid plans), or your data vendor's CSV download. TradeAtlas ships no licensed live feed.
timestamp,open,high,low,close,volume (aliases like Date/AAPL.Close are converted by you before upload; UNIX seconds or ISO dates both parse).

data_guide.step: 3. Decide adjusted vs raw — and write it down
data_guide.detail: Splits/dividends make raw series jump. State which you used; results from mixed series are not comparable.
Daily bars honestly support only 1d/1w here. Nobody can reconstruct 5-minute history from daily bars; anyone who claims otherwise is fabricating data.

data_guide.step: 5. Judge forecasters out-of-sample or not at all
data_guide.detail: Use the Forecast Lab's rolling evaluation: hide the future, forecast, check, repeat 100 times, and demand it beat always-up/momentum baselines before believing any 'edge' — then re-test on a second symbol and era.

paper_wallet.demo_crypto_balances: The v13 demo e-wallet can hold imaginary USDT/USDC/BTC/ETH/SOL quantities, convert those imaginary balances to PAPER_USD at a user-typed rate, simulate a withdrawal by deleting imaginary units, and move PAPER_USD internally to/from the paper bot. None of those actions touches a blockchain, bank, exchange or real asset.
paper_wallet.external_account_mirror: v14 can record balances that the user says are held in the user's OWN licensed exchange/broker account. This is an unverified accounting mirror only: TradeAtlas cannot access, verify, receive, convert, withdraw or trade those assets, and mirrored balances are excluded from paper equity.
paper_wallet.what_simulated_conversion_means: A user types a hypothetical crypto amount and a hypothetical USD rate; TradeAtlas adds the product to an imaginary PAPER_USD balance. Nothing is received, converted, custodied, withdrawn or traded for real.
paper_wallet.follow_mode: When following is ON, one follow-step may create a simulated spot position from the latest completed supplied bar. STOP sets a hard halt that blocks new paper-follow actions. Spot paper wallet is long-only: a short condition exits a simulated holding; it never opens a real or leveraged short.
paper_wallet.warning: Never send cryptocurrency or money to TradeAtlas. It has no deposit address and cannot convert or trade real assets.

halal_screen.purpose: A transparent, user-configurable stock screen for the paper bot. It is software arithmetic on data the user supplies, NOT a fatwa and NOT a certification that any security is halal.
halal_screen.bot_rule: The bot may open a paper position only when asset_type is stock and the registered screen status is exactly pass. Missing data is needs_review, never pass.
important_limits: Standards differ between scholars, indices and jurisdictions; choose the preset/thresholds you personally follow.
TradeAtlas does not fetch or verify company accounts. Wrong or stale user inputs produce a wrong screen.
A pass can expire when newer financial statements arrive; re-screen periodically.
Dividend purification methods differ; any estimate shown must be checked with your chosen standard.

halal_paper_bot.universe: registered assets whose current user-supplied halal screen status is pass (stocks use financial ratios; other classes require explicit spot/no-interest/no-leverage evidence)
halal_paper_bot.execution: paper fills only; optional manual external-account checklist tickets are generated but never sent. No broker/exchange credentials, automatic real order, leverage, margin or short selling exists in TradeAtlas.

allocation cap and maximum open positions

goals.evidence: Allowlisted public-venue collector (server CLI and browser), incremental SQLite storage with provenance, holdout reservation with a recorded access count, pooled evidence and a gate-by-gate goal report.

goals.title: Learn from every failed test instead of repeating it
goals.evidence: A cause library of 20 named failure modes, an avoid-rule and an implemented remedy per cause, a three-stage loop (screen -> apply lessons -> validate), resolved/recurred/retired lesson states, and a SQLite failure memory that makes later runs skip already-proven dead candidates.
goals.not_claimed: The failure memory improves the *research process*, not the market. It cannot create an edge that the sample does not contain, and it never lowers the 80% gates.

market_lab.disclaimer: Educational/research output only — not financial advice and not a recommendation. Mechanical indicator conditions can be wrong, historical accuracy does not predict future results, and most short-term traders lose money. Verify data rights, costs, liquidity, taxes and broker rules independently; consider paper trading first.

failure_memory.name: Atlas Failure Memory — self-correcting research loop
loop: screen every method x horizon on completed bars
diagnose each failure against an explicit cause library
turn every cause into an avoid-rule plus an implemented remedy
re-test only what can still be saved, with the avoid-rules applied
resolved -> keep the fix; recurred -> retire and remember
validate survivors on the recent slice and a second symbol

cause_library.title: Not enough history to place any test origin
cause_library.meaning: The series is shorter than the warm-up plus the horizon, so nothing could be scored.
cause_library.avoid: Never report a rate from a series that cannot produce at least 20 separated origins.
cause_library.remedy: Import a longer lawful series; do not lower the warm-up to manufacture attempts.

cause_library.title: The method abstained on every origin
cause_library.meaning: Every origin score was zero/missing, so the method made no call to evaluate.
cause_library.avoid: A method that never speaks must not be ranked as if it were accurate.
cause_library.remedy: Relax the abstention threshold (threshold scale 0) once, and retire the method if it still never speaks.

cause_library.title: Too few attempts for the verdict
cause_library.meaning: Fewer attempts than the configured screen minimum were produced.
cause_library.avoid: Do not generalise from a handful of attempts; small samples swing by chance alone.
cause_library.remedy: Raise the attempt budget (more separated origins), and retire the candidate if the series cannot supply them.

cause_library.title: Too selective to be useful
cause_library.meaning: The method spoke on too small a share of origins; a high rate on a tiny slice is not a strategy.
cause_library.avoid: Always publish accuracy next to coverage; a filtered subset is not a full-coverage claim.
cause_library.remedy: Lower the score threshold (threshold scale 0) and re-test coverage before believing the rate.

cause_library.title: Below the 80% project target
cause_library.meaning: Direction accuracy is below the project's stated 80% target.
cause_library.avoid: Never present a below-target number as if the target had been reached.
cause_library.remedy: Keep the honest gap visible; the target is a research goal, not a parameter to tune.

cause_library.title: No directional edge at all
cause_library.meaning: Accuracy is at or below a coin flip on this sample.
cause_library.avoid: Do not dress up a coin flip with extra indicators or a new name.
cause_library.remedy: Retire this candidate on this series; an ensemble of its cousins is not a fix.

cause_library.title: A naive baseline is at least as good
cause_library.meaning: Always-up or 5-bar momentum matched or beat the method.
cause_library.avoid: Always print the naive baselines in the same table; a method must beat them to matter.
cause_library.remedy: Retire the candidate and keep the baseline as the reference: if always-up/momentum wins, the method adds nothing here.

cause_library.title: Gross edge disappeared after costs
cause_library.meaning: The mean gross move was positive but the net after round-trip cost was not.
cause_library.avoid: Never quote gross accuracy or gross return as tradable; costs are part of the result.
cause_library.remedy: Trade only when the causal expected move is at least 2x the round-trip cost, then re-test.

cause_library.title: The cost filter removed too much of the sample
cause_library.meaning: The cost-aware filter skipped most origins, leaving too few attempts to judge anything.
cause_library.avoid: A remedy that starves its own sample is not a fix; check coverage after every filter.
cause_library.remedy: Relax the filter one step (>= 1.0x cost) and re-measure; retire if even that starves coverage.

cause_library.title: Negative expectancy after costs
cause_library.meaning: The mean net result per attempt is negative after the configured cost.
cause_library.avoid: A negative-expectancy method is not made positive by describing it better.
cause_library.remedy: Retire the candidate; report the loss instead of hiding it.

cause_library.title: Edge lives in one horizon cell only
cause_library.meaning: Neighbouring horizons collapsed, which is the classic signature of a cherry-picked cell.
cause_library.avoid: Test neighbouring horizons in the same run and demand agreement before calling anything an edge.
cause_library.remedy: Require the neighbouring horizons to stay within 8 points, then re-test.

cause_library.title: The later slice is worse than the earlier slice
cause_library.meaning: Accuracy dropped sharply between the earlier and later part of the sample.
cause_library.avoid: A single pooled number hides decay; always split early vs late.
cause_library.remedy: Judge the candidate on the recent slice only and require a positive recent edge.

cause_library.title: Edge depends on one market regime
cause_library.meaning: One causal regime carried the result while another lost money.
cause_library.avoid: Do not pool regimes silently, and never pick the winning regime after seeing the result.
cause_library.remedy: Require both regimes to be non-losing and report them separately, then re-test.

cause_library.title: Path drawdown beyond the limit
cause_library.meaning: The cumulative net path fell further than the allowed drawdown.
cause_library.avoid: Accuracy without a drawdown number is half a result.
cause_library.remedy: Skip thin-edge trades (expected move >= 1.5x cost) and re-measure the path.

cause_library.title: Confidence interval too wide to conclude anything
cause_library.meaning: The Wilson 95% interval is wide enough to contain both an edge and its opposite.
cause_library.avoid: Never call a point estimate significant while its interval spans 50%.
cause_library.remedy: Increase attempts; if the sample cannot grow, keep the label unproven.

cause_library.title: Only one symbol was supplied
cause_library.meaning: The result comes from a single series and cannot be generalised.
cause_library.avoid: One symbol is a case study, never a market law.
cause_library.remedy: Validate on a second lawful series before upgrading the label.

cause_library.title: Series too short for a stable estimate
cause_library.meaning: The bar count cannot support the warm-up, horizon and attempt budget together.
cause_library.avoid: Do not shrink the warm-up to make a short series look evaluable.
cause_library.remedy: Supply more history; otherwise keep the candidate retired.

cause_library.title: Winner chosen among many contestants
cause_library.meaning: This candidate is the best of several raced in the same round, so its number is inflated by selection.
cause_library.avoid: The top row of a tournament is the most over-fitted row; label it as such.
cause_library.remedy: Confirm on a held-out slice and a second symbol before any claim.

cause_library.title: Volume-based method on a volume-less series
cause_library.meaning: The method needs real traded volume but every bar reports zero.
cause_library.avoid: Never invent volume to satisfy an indicator.
cause_library.remedy: Retire the volume method for this series; use a price-only method instead.

cause_library.title: Cost assumption below the research floor
cause_library.meaning: The configured round-trip cost is below the minimum floor used for research.
cause_library.avoid: Zero-cost tests flatter every high-frequency idea; assume at least the floor.
cause_library.remedy: Raise the cost assumption to the floor and re-score.

cause_library.title: The remedy was applied and the cause returned
cause_library.meaning: The candidate failed again for the same reason after its remedy was applied.
cause_library.avoid: Do not retry a proven-failing candidate with cosmetic changes; remember and exclude it.
cause_library.remedy: Retire the candidate and keep the lesson as a permanent avoid rule for later runs.

verdicts.validated_on_supplied_data_still_needs_f: survived the supplied screen, recent slice and second symbol (if any)
verdicts.survived_the_recent_slice_but_a_second_s: held up on the recent slice of one symbol only — still a case study, not a law
verdicts.all_candidates_excluded_by_prior_lessons: stored lessons already retired every requested candidate for this symbol
verdicts.no_candidate_survived_validation: nothing held up out of sample on the supplied data
verdicts.no_candidate_survived_the_failure_gates: every candidate failed a blocker cause and was retired with a reason

limits: Research only; not financial advice and not a live execution path.
The 80% target can never be established by this module alone.
A retired candidate is a measured negative result, not a bug.

data_pipeline.name: Atlas Auto-Collect + Goal Tracker
security: fixed host allowlist; no arbitrary URLs
no API keys, logins or credentials
read-only market data; no order routing

goal_gates.requirement: at least 1000 hidden-future attempts per candidate
positive mean net per attempt after 10 bps
coverage at least 20% when the method can abstain
a recorded holdout evaluation on the reserved slice
fresh unseen validation outside this local database

market_database.seed: bundled real AAPL daily + five monthly samples; expand only with data you have the right to use
market_database.private_access: Set TRADEATLAS_ACCESS_TOKEN to require X-TradeAtlas-Token on paper/bot/halal/database APIs; bind to localhost for a private local platform
